summary: Day 1 of the 5-session test went the way of the risk-off call (0.55), but not by enough to settle it. The SPY benchmark value fell from 565.41 to 562.66 (about -0.49%), well short of the -1% that grades risk-off right, with two shortened holiday sessions (closed 11-26, half day 11-27) still to come. The book ended at 615.73 (+3.88 on the day, +0.63%) while about 50% sat in cash, so low equity appetite held up. The weak spot is the duration call. TLT fell 0.38% on a down day for stocks (mark 81.49 against the 81.69 packet close and the 81.698 fill). That was less than SPY's drop, but it was not the rally I described as 'the one sleeve working'. The held Staples names did not drag (KR +4.42%, SAM +0.29%), and Health Care, which I did not favor, led the book (INCY +5.33%, IDXX +3.65%). These are single-name moves, not sector evidence.
broken_theses: Duration as the hedge to lean on: on the first session after the call, TLT fell 0.38% while the SPY benchmark fell about 0.49%. It lost less than equities but did not rise against them, which was the flight-to-quality pattern (TLT 5d +2.91% vs SPY 5d -2.39%) my note was built on. One day does not break it, and TLT's stored relative clause (TLT 5d below SPY 5d in a down week) is not met on this evidence. Still, the PM sized the third TLT buy in four sessions on my sentence 'Treasuries are the one sleeve working', and that rested on one week of evidence while TLT was still 1.11% under its 200-day.
update: Keep risk-off for now. The grade is open: SPY needs about another -0.5% over four thin sessions to reach -1%, and a quiet holiday week makes neutral a real risk. My graded record is 0.55 against a 0.50 always-risk-off baseline, and all three recent misses were risk-on calls (11-10, 11-11, 11-16). So I will not flip without a measured turn: VIXY 5d negative with SPY back above its 200-day (730.47 as of 11-23). For tomorrow, check whether TLT's 5d return is still above SPY's. If TLT gives back its gains while SPY falls, I will drop the 'lean on duration' language and say outright that the Treasury sleeve is not hedging, since the PM's TLT clause and sizing depend on that sentence. I could not check HYG, VIXY or sector ETFs from close.json, so the credit counter-evidence stays as it was. No active lesson names the market-analyst.
